figures.caption: Figure 1. Integrated design framework for ultrathin composite solid electrolytes (UCSEs) in all-solid-state lithium batteries. UCSE performance arises from the coupled optimization of electrolyte thickness, lithium-ion transport architecture, mechanical integrity, interfacial stability, dendrite resistance, and scalable manufacturability. The synergy among these design principles enables high ionic conductivity, enhanced safety, long-term cycling durability, a wide electrochemical stability window, and practical high-energy-density solid- state batteries. The figure is formed by using powerpoint.

figures.caption: Figure 6. Mechanism of lithium dendrite propagation and mechanical failure in solid electrolytes. Non-uniform lithium deposition generates localized stress that promotes dendrite nucleation, crack initiation, and crack- assisted dendrite propagation through the electrolyte, ultimately leading to internal short circuits. The lower panel illustrates the origins of mechanical failure, including volume expansion, stress concentration at structural defects, and crack growth, together with the mitigating effect of mechanically reinforced electrolyte frameworks that redistribute stress and suppress dendrite penetration.

figures.caption: Figure 7. Electrode–electrolyte interfaces and artificial interlayers in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Direct contact between solid electrolytes and electrodes promotes interfacial decomposition, impedance growth, and dendrite formation, whereas artificial interlayers stabilize both anode–electrolyte and cathode–electrolyte interfaces by suppressing side reactions, reducing interfacial resistance, and improving lithium-ion transport and long-term electrochemical stability.
